hsk30l3/春天.why: Found by READING the card (batch 26): two independent clauses run together with no mark between them — 冬天结束了春天已经来了 — so the sentence reads as one and the speaker gives it no pause. The repair supplies the clause comma and changes no word, which is what `exSpace` is bounded to.
exSpace: 冬天结束了春天已经来了。
冬天结束了，春天已经来了。

hsk30l3/蛋糕.why: Found by READING the card (batch 26): the English asserted more than the Chinese. 不同一般 is 'out of the ordinary', a judgement of unusualness; the card rendered it 'The cake tastes divine!', which asserts deliciousness the sentence does not. The Chinese is untouched.
exEn: 这蛋糕吃起来不同一般。
This cake tastes out of the ordinary.

hsk30l3/大小.why: The gloss was not the sense the card's own examples show (batch 26). 大小 was glossed 'dimension' and all three sentences mean SIZE — 'the same size', 'size 10 shoes', 'the size of an egg' — while CC-CEDICT gives 'large and small; size; adults and children'. 'dimension' reads in English as a measurement along one axis, which is not what the word means. The parenthetical is a DISAMBIGUATOR rather than a note about the card: 尺寸 is already glossed 'size; dimensions; measurements (esp. of clothes)', so a bare 'size' would have put two cards a reader cannot tell apart on the reverse deck.

hsk30l3/出生.why: A noun gloss stood under a verb label (batch 26): 出生 was glossed 'birth; to be born' as a verb, and CC-CEDICT gives only 'to be born'. All three examples are the verb. 诞生 keeps its own 'be born; come into being; emerge', which is what still tells the two apart on the reverse card.

hsk30l3/带.why: A measure word pointed at a sense the card never gave (batch 26). 带 was glossed 'carry' under a 'noun / verb' label and carried the classifier 条, which counts the NOUN — a belt or a strap — so the card promised a countable noun and defined none. This is the measure-word family where the two-part-of-speech flag really is a missing sense rather than one meaning wearing two labels; the 1,510 notes carrying that flag are NOT swept, and this one was read. CC-CEDICT gives both halves. No `exSense`: all three examples are the verb, and a tag repeating itself three times says nothing.

hsk30l3/东.why: Found by READING the card (batch 27): NOT ONE of the three sentences used the word the card teaches. 东 is glossed 'east' and the examples were 东西 dōngxi 'thing', 广东 Guǎngdōng the province, and 东家 dōngjiā 'landlord' — three different words that merely begin with the character. This is `check-example-fit.js`'s stated blind spot twice over: a SINGLE-CHARACTER headword is skipped by that tool outright, and two of the three sentences segment cleanly anyway. The replacement is AUTHORED, and the record says so: short, ordinary, and using the word in the sense the card's own gloss gives it, in a construction the card's other two sentences do not already use. The three replacements give 东 its three ordinary free uses — after 往, after 朝, and as a bare predicate noun in a question. (The second sentence, 来广东玩吗, also carried no final mark at all.)
ex: 往东走五分钟就到车站了。
Walk east for five minutes and you reach the station.
The windows of my house face east.
Excuse me, which way is east?

hsk30l3/发.why: Found by READING the card (batch 27): the first sentence was about a DIFFERENT WORD AND A DIFFERENT READING. 我喜欢短发 is duǎnfà 'short hair', which in traditional script is 短髮 — a separate character from the card's own 發 — so a learner met the headword's shape carrying neither its sound nor its sense. Single-character headwords are skipped by `check-example-fit.js`, so nothing in the pipeline could see it. The replacement is AUTHORED, and the record says so: short, ordinary, and using the word in the sense the card's own gloss gives it, in a construction the card's other two sentences do not already use. The gloss went with it: 'to send (an email)' narrowed the word to one object and the parenthetical was a note about the card rather than a disambiguator. CC-CEDICT gives 發 fā as 'to send out; to issue; to develop', and the card's other two sentences are 发短信 and 发问, which the narrow gloss did not cover.

hsk30l3/耳朵.why: Found by READING the card (batch 27): the first sentence was a half-quoted retort. 我长耳朵了 stands on its own as 'I have grown ears'; the thing people actually say is 我又不是没长耳朵, and the card's English ('I have ears, you know.') was translating the idiom rather than the sentence. The replacement is AUTHORED, and the record says so: short, ordinary, and using the word in the sense the card's own gloss gives it, in a construction the card's other two sentences do not already use. The gloss went from 'ears' to 'ear' on the same card: it carries the classifiers 只 and 个, which count ONE ear, so the card was promising a countable noun and glossing a plural. Measured across the nine decks, single-word noun glosses run 1,005 singular to 61 plural, and most of that 61 is English that has no singular — trousers, chopsticks, news. This is not swept: 动物 in the same batch is the other countable one in range, and the rest were left alone.

hsk30l3/饿.why: Found by READING the card (batch 27): the sentence was UNGRAMMATICAL. 我总是饿了 puts the change-of-state 了 under 总是 'always', and a state that is always true cannot also be a change into it — 我总是很饿 or 我老是饿 is what is said. The replacement is AUTHORED, and the record says so: short, ordinary, and using the word in the sense the card's own gloss gives it, in a construction the card's other two sentences do not already use. The A-not-A question is a construction neither of the other two sentences uses.

hsk30l3/发生.why: Found by READING the card (batch 27): the third sentence was UNGRAMMATICAL: 这件事突然自己发生的 is a 是…的 cleft with the 是 missing, so the sentence ends on a 的 that nothing licenses. The replacement uses the existential 发生了一件… , which is how the word is most often met and which neither other sentence shows. The replacement is AUTHORED, and the record says so: short, ordinary, and using the word in the sense the card's own gloss gives it, in a construction the card's other two sentences do not already use. The second sentence's English, 'May it not happen!', is an optative nobody writes; the Chinese is an ordinary 希望.
dropEx: 这件事突然自己发生的。
ex: 昨天晚上发生了一件奇怪的事。
exEn: 希望它不会发生
I hope it doesn't happen.

hsk30l3/短.why: Found by READING the card (batch 27): the sentence was a word-for-word calque of its own English. 短回答是是 is 'The short answer is yes' rendered character by character; Chinese has no attributive 短回答, and the doubled 是是 reads as a stammer. The replacement is AUTHORED, and the record says so: short, ordinary, and using the word in the sense the card's own gloss gives it, in a construction the card's other two sentences do not already use. The replacement is the comparative, which is the construction an adjective card most needs and which the card did not have.
ex: This road is shorter than that one.

hsk30l3/而且.why: Found by READING the card (batch 27): the second sentence repeated its subject three times — 我有钱，我胖而且我快乐 — to carry an English list of three adjectives, which is not what 而且 does: it joins CLAUSES, and Chinese does not restate 我 in front of each. The replacement is AUTHORED, and the record says so: short, ordinary, and using the word in the sense the card's own gloss gives it, in a construction the card's other two sentences do not already use. The replacement joins a clause to a degree complement, so the card's three sentences now show 不但…而且, a verb clause and an adjective clause rather than two of the last. The third sentence's English ('It was cold, and in addition, it was windy.') was stilted and put an unmarked sentence in the past.
dropEx: 我有钱，我胖而且我快乐。
ex: 他会说中文，而且说得很好。
He speaks Chinese, and he speaks it well.
exEn: 天气很冷，而且风很大
It's cold, and very windy too.

hsk30l3/动物.why: Found by READING the card (batch 27): the gloss was plural on a card carrying the classifiers 只 and 群, which count one animal and one herd — so the card promised a countable noun and defined a mass of them. CC-CEDICT gives 'animal'. Measured across the nine decks, single-word noun glosses run 1,005 singular to 61 plural, and most of that 61 is English with no singular (trousers, chopsticks, news, maths); this is NOT swept — 耳朵 is the other countable one inside this batch's range and the rest were left where they stand.

hsk30l3/发烧.why: Found by READING the card (batch 27): a verb glossed with a noun first. 发烧 is 'to have a fever' and the gloss opened on 'fever', which is 烧 or 发热 as a noun and is not what any of the three sentences says. CC-CEDICT: 'to have a high temperature (from illness); to have a fever'.

hsk30l3/对话.why: Found by READING the card (batch 27): the part of speech and the gloss contradicted each other: the card said 'verb' and defined 'dialogue', a noun, and all three of its sentences are the noun — 参与对话, 我们的对话, 维持一段对话. CC-CEDICT gives both halves, 'to talk (with sb)' and 'dialogue; conversation', so the repair is to state the sense the card was already teaching and keep the verb the label was pointing at. No `exSense`: all three examples are the noun, and a tag repeating itself three times says nothing. | The AMERICAN -LOGUE FORMS ARE INVISIBLE TO `check-british.js`, because they are invisible to app.js's own `SPELL_PAIRS` (batch 27): the -logue family is one of the five CLAUDE.md names as deliberately absent from that table, so the checker reports zero over the whole corpus while these stand. Measured: the nine decks carry exactly TWO, one in this batch's range and one outside it, and both are repaired here rather than left to reopen as a class. Two is also why this is not a deck-level pass — `exLexis` exists for a substitution worth applying in one place, and a table of one word applied twice is a table nobody will read. On this card it also contradicted the card's own gloss, which the same batch rewrote to 'dialogue; conversation'.
exEn: 我没有参与对话
I did not take part in the dialogue.

hsk30l3/段.why: Found by READING the card (batch 27): the gloss was CUT OFF MID-BRACKET — 'section; paragraph; [measure word for stories, pieces' — so the card ended on an open bracket and an unfinished list. Rewritten to the two senses CC-CEDICT gives ('paragraph/section/segment' and the classifier), in the shape the deck's other measure-word cards use, e.g. 条's '(for long thin things: roads, fish, trousers)'. All three of the card's English translations were wrong as well: 一段时间 with 看 is watching rather than looking after, 一段 is a paragraph and not a sentence, and 我跟你说段历史 offers a piece of history rather than reporting a conversation. No `exSense`: all three sentences are the classifier.
senses: a paragraph; a section; a stretch
(for stretches of road or time, and for pieces of writing)
exEn: 我看了他一段时间
I watched him for a while.
每人读一段
Each of you read a paragraph.
我跟你说段历史
Let me tell you a bit of history.

hsk30l3/发现.why: Found by READING the card (batch 27): 你家很容易发现 uses 发现 for finding a PLACE, which it does not do — a house one can find easily is 很好找 or 很容易找到, where 发现 is noticing or discovering something one was not looking for. The replacement is AUTHORED, and the record says so: short, ordinary, and using the word in the sense the card's own gloss gives it, in a construction the card's other two sentences do not already use. The replacement gives the card the 'become aware' half of the word, which CC-CEDICT lists first and which none of the three sentences showed.

hsk30l3/发展.why: Found by READING the card (batch 27): the first and third sentences were the same sentence twice — 中国发展得很快 and 中国很快地发展, same subject, same claim, and the second of them stilted, a bare 很快地 before 发展 wanting a 得 complement instead. The replacement is AUTHORED, and the record says so: short, ordinary, and using the word in the sense the card's own gloss gives it, in a construction the card's other two sentences do not already use. The replacement is the TRANSITIVE use, which the card did not have at all. The second sentence's English called it 'high speed development'.
exEn: 他们都享受那么快的发展吗
Do they all enjoy such rapid development?

hsk30l3/方便.why: Found by READING the card (batch 27): the English was not what the Chinese says. 'Convenient to public transportation' is not English anybody writes, and 交通不方便 is about how hard the place is to reach.
exEn: 这地方交通不方便
This place isn't easy to get to by public transport.

hsk30l3/方法.why: Found by READING the card (batch 27): the English was not what the Chinese says. The Chinese is active and carries 找到; the English turned it passive and dropped the finding.
exEn: 我们希望找到解决方法
We hope to find a solution.

hsk30l3/方向.why: Found by READING the card (batch 27): the English was not what the Chinese says. 'I've mistaken the direction' is not idiomatic; 搞错 is getting a thing wrong.
exEn: 我把方向搞错了
Sorry, I got the direction wrong.

hsk30l3/服务.why: Found by READING the card (batch 28): the same blind spot, and a missing sense behind it. The third sentence was 服务生，买单 — 服务生 is a WAITER, so the characters are there and the word is not; 服务生 is not a headword in these decks, so the segmenter lands on 服务 and `check-example-fit.js` sees nothing. Reading the card also showed the gloss was half of it: 服务 was labelled VERB and defined 'to serve' while the second sentence, 我们不需要你的服务, is the noun, and the card carries the classifier 项, which counts the noun. CC-CEDICT gives both. The replacement is AUTHORED, and the record says so: short, ordinary, and using the word in the sense the card's own gloss gives it, in a construction the card's other two sentences do not already use. The replacement shows the noun, so the card's three sentences now divide 1/2/2 and carry an `exSense` that says so.
ex: The service at this restaurant is very good.

hsk30l3/感到.why: Found by READING the card (batch 28): the sentence read two ways and neither was good. 我为人生感到很开心 is meant as 为 + 人生, but 为人 wéirén is itself a word and the decks' own segmenter takes it that way — and even read as intended, 为…感到 wants a specific cause rather than life at large. Its English, 'I get a kick out of life', was slang for a sentence that carries none. The replacement is AUTHORED, and the record says so: short, ordinary, and using the word in the sense the card's own gloss gives it, in a construction the card's other two sentences do not already use. The replacement gives 感到 the cause clause the construction actually takes.
ex: 听到这个消息，我感到很意外。
I was very surprised when I heard the news.

hsk30l3/感兴趣.why: Found by READING the card (batch 28): the sentence was a 是…的 cleft carrying a plain English translation. 他是对我感兴趣的 singles out WHO he is interested in, where 'He was interested in me' singles out nothing — so the card taught an emphatic construction as if it were the ordinary one. The replacement is AUTHORED, and the record says so: short, ordinary, and using the word in the sense the card's own gloss gives it, in a construction the card's other two sentences do not already use. The replacement is the ordinary statement, which the card did not have: its other two sentences are a negative and a question.
ex: He is very interested in history.

hsk30l3/公斤.why: Found by READING the card (batch 28): the second and third sentences were one question asked twice — 一公斤香蕉多少钱 and 香蕉多少钱一公斤, the same words in two orders — and the third's English, 'How much is the kilo of bananas?', is not English anybody speaks. The replacement is AUTHORED, and the record says so: short, ordinary, and using the word in the sense the card's own gloss gives it, in a construction the card's other two sentences do not already use. The replacement is the weight-of-a-thing construction rather than a third price.
ex: 这个箱子有二十公斤重。

hsk30l3/放.why: Found by READING the card (batch 28): the gloss changed grammar half way through: 'to put; set free' gives an infinitive and then a bare imperative, so the two halves read as different kinds of word. CC-CEDICT gives 'to put; to place; to release; to free; to let go'.
hsk30l3/放.gloss: to put; to place; to let go

hsk30l3/感冒.why: Found by READING the card (batch 28): the measure-word family again, and the same tell batch 26 found on 带: the card said 'noun / verb' and gave one VERB gloss while carrying the classifiers 场 and 次, which count the noun — a cold, a bout of one. Its own third sentence, 感冒真难受, is that noun. CC-CEDICT gives both halves. The three sentences divide 1/1/2, so this one earns an `exSense` where 带's did not. Its English also said 'It sucks having a cold', which is American slang for a sentence that is plain Chinese.
exEn: 感冒真难受
Having a cold is really miserable.

hsk30l3/根据.why: Found by READING the card (batch 28): the card named THREE parts of speech against one gloss, and the gloss was the third of them: 'according to' is the preposition, while two of the card's three sentences are the NOUN — 有没有根据, 'have you any grounds', and 是根据什么, 'what is the basis'. The classifier 个 it carries counts that noun. CC-CEDICT gives 'according to; based on; basis; foundation'. The three sentences genuinely divide 1/3/1, so this one carries an `exSense`.
senses: according to; on the basis of

hsk30l3/关.why: Found by READING the card (batch 28): the card said 'noun / verb' and gave one gloss, 'to close' — and its own third sentence, 不关你的事, is a DIFFERENT VERB, the 关 of concerning somebody, which the card never defined. So a reader met a use the card had not taught, on the card itself. CC-CEDICT gives the three: to close, to concern, and the noun — a mountain pass, which is what the 'noun' label had been promising with nothing behind it. `exSense` marks which sentence is which.
senses: to close; to shut; to turn off

hsk30l3/放心.why: Found by READING the card (batch 28): the English was not what the Chinese says. 放心 is being reassured, and the first sentence's English opened 'Come on', which is chivvying somebody along — the opposite thing to say. The third's 'You can rely upon his being punctual' is a construction no one writes.
exEn: 放心，没事的
Don't worry, it'll be all right.
你可以放心，他会准时的
You can rest assured — he'll be on time.

hsk30l3/分开.why: Found by READING the card (batch 28): the English was not what the Chinese says. The Chinese says two questions must be discussed separately; the English turned it into one question discussed apart from another, which is a different arrangement of the same words.
exEn: 这两个问题必须分开讨论
These two questions must be discussed separately.

hsk30l3/附近.why: Found by READING the card (batch 28): the English was not what the Chinese says. 'Near by' as two words is not the adverb; it is also the card's own gloss written wrong on the card's own first sentence.
exEn: 附近有个车站
There's a bus stop nearby.

hsk30l3/刚才.why: Found by READING the card (batch 28): the English was not what the Chinese says. Both English lines dropped 刚才, which is the whole of what the card teaches — 'I was at home' and 'Who is the man that you were talking with' would translate the sentences with the headword taken out. The second also made 人 a man.
exEn: 我刚才在家
I was at home just now.
刚才和你说话的人是谁？
Who was that you were talking to just now?

hsk30l3/刮.why: Found by READING the card (batch 28): the English was not what the Chinese says. 刮起来 is being lifted into the air; 'The papers blew off' says they came off something, which the sentence does not.
exEn: 文件被风刮起来
The papers were sent flying by the wind.

hsk30l3/关系.why: Found by READING the card (batch 29): the card named two parts of speech and gave one gloss, and the gloss was the noun's — so its own third sentence, 不只是钱关系重大, was the VERB sense (to concern, to matter) with nothing on the card defining it. Batch 28's shape exactly. Both senses are CC-CEDICT's, in its order. The second sentence's English was also in the past tense over a present-tense Chinese.
exEn: 我们的关系非常好
Our relationship is very good.

hsk30l3/关注.why: Found by READING the card (batch 29): the card named one part of speech, verb, and its FIRST sentence was the noun — 谢谢您的关注, 'thank you for your attention' — a sense the card nowhere defined. CC-CEDICT carries both. The second sentence's English, 'he doesn't care much for baseball', said 关心 rather than 关注.
exEn: 他不太关注棒球
He doesn't pay much attention to baseball.

hsk30l3/好多.why: Found by READING the card (batch 29): the card glossed 'many' and its first sentence, 这样好多了, means 'this is much better' — a second sense CC-CEDICT lists outright (/many/quite a lot/much better/) and the card did not. It is NOT a straddle `check-example-fit.js` could have caught: the segmenter lands squarely on 好多. The sense is recorded rather than the sentence dropped, because the sentence is a real and common use of the word — though it is worth knowing that most grammars parse 好多了 as 好 + 多了 rather than 好多 + 了, and CC-CEDICT is what settles it here. The `not 许多` reverse-card hint is retired with the same edit and its row removed from `hints`: the first sense now reads 'many; quite a lot' where 许多 reads 'many', so the two no longer collide and a disambiguator disambiguating nothing is worse than none.

hsk30l3/或者.why: Found by READING the card (batch 29): the card's only gloss was 'perhaps' and all three of its sentences mean 'or' — so the commonest sense of one of the commonest words in the language was missing from its own card. CC-CEDICT leads with /or/ and gives possibly/maybe/perhaps second. The conjunction is deliberately glossed 'or; either ... or' rather than a bare 'or': three other cards (或, 或是, 要么) already carry the bare word, and the house rule gives a group of three or more distinguishing glosses rather than a `not X` hint.

hsk30l3/回答.why: Found by READING the card (batch 29): the card glossed 'reply' and all three of its sentences answer a QUESTION — 请回答问题, 这个问题很容易回答. CC-CEDICT gives /to reply; to answer/. The collocation is what distinguishes it and is written into the gloss, because the bare 'to answer; to reply' is already 应对's gloss word for word and a fourth card glossed 'answer' would be a reverse-card question with two right answers.

hsk30l3/环境.why: Found by READING the card (batch 29): the card glossed 'environment' alone, and two of its three sentences use the word in the wider sense CC-CEDICT also carries (/environment/circumstances/surroundings/): 我适应新环境很慢 and 我需要换个环境, whose English said 'new situations' and 'a change of scenery' and so taught the reader nothing about the word on the card. The gloss is widened and the first sentence's English put back on the headword; the third is left as it stands, 'a change of scenery' being the idiomatic English for it and now covered by the gloss.
exEn: 我适应新环境很慢
I'm slow to adapt to a new environment.

hsk30l3/海.why: Found by READING the card (batch 29): two of the card's three sentences used the character and not the word: 人山人海 is an idiom (a sea of people) and 海带 is kelp, so a card glossed 'sea' showed a crowd and a vegetable. Batch 27's 东 finding again — `check-example-fit.js` skips a single-character headword outright, so neither is reportable. The replacement is AUTHORED, and the record says so: short, ordinary, and using the word in the sense the card's own gloss gives it, in a construction the card's other two sentences do not already use. | The card glosses its character and stops, and the tap panel that would list the other words built on it can only search the deck the reader has downloaded. AUTHORED, and the record says so. Candidates come from the corpus where it has them and from CC-CEDICT where its words are too few or too advanced for the level, and EVERY row's reading and gloss was checked against CC-CEDICT before it was written.
ex: This city is very close to the sea.
The sea is deep and I do not dare go in.

hsk30l3/国家.why: Found by READING the card (batch 29): 你是哪国家？ is not grammatical: 哪 needs its classifier before a noun, and the sentence needs a head for 的 to hang on. The repair keeps what the sentence was teaching — asking someone where they are from — in the form a speaker would use. The replacement is AUTHORED, and the record says so: short, ordinary, and using the word in the sense the card's own gloss gives it, in a construction the card's other two sentences do not already use.
ex: Which country do you come from?

hsk30l3/黄色.why: Found by READING the card (batch 29): 红色和黄色和蓝色 chains 和 the way English chains 'and', which Chinese does not do: a list takes the enumeration comma 、 between its members and 和 before the last one only. The replacement is AUTHORED, and the record says so: short, ordinary, and using the word in the sense the card's own gloss gives it, in a construction the card's other two sentences do not already use. The replacement is attributive, where the card's other two sentences are an object and a 是…的 predicate.
dropEx: 红色和黄色和蓝色是颜色。
ex: Please give me the yellow notebook.

hsk30l3/换.why: The card glosses its character and stops, and the tap panel that would list the other words built on it can only search the deck the reader has downloaded. AUTHORED, and the record says so. Candidates come from the corpus where it has them and from CC-CEDICT where its words are too few or too advanced for the level, and EVERY row's reading and gloss was checked against CC-CEDICT before it was written.

hsk30l3/关于.why: Found by READING the card (batch 29): six ASCII full stops where Chinese writes the ellipsis ……. It is the deck-level punctuation pass's own class — a half-width mark inside a Chinese sentence — and the pass cannot see it: its table converts , ; : ! ? and pairs quotes, and has no row for the full stop, the full stop being a legitimate mark inside a number. Measured over all nine decks the class is SEVEN sentences over five decks against four that use …… correctly, and two of the seven (郊区很安静... and 倾听...) are not sentences at all but truncated fragments needing judgement — so it is not a table, and this one is repaired where it stands. The other six are recorded in docs/mandarin-review.md for the batches that reach them.
exSpace: 关于这件事......我真的不知道。
关于这件事……我真的不知道。

hsk30l3/关心.why: Found by READING the card (batch 29): the English was not what the Chinese says. 'He is careless about money' says he is bad with money; 不关心 says he does not care about it.
exEn: 他不关心钱
He doesn't care about money.

hsk30l3/害怕.why: Found by READING the card (batch 29): the English was not what the Chinese says. 'She never shivers' is a translation of something else entirely, and the card is glossed 'afraid'.
exEn: 她从不害怕
She is never afraid.

hsk30l3/好像.why: Found by READING the card (batch 29): the English was not what the Chinese says. 'How fascinating!' renders 挺有趣 and drops the headword, so the one word the card is teaching had nothing standing for it in the English.

Replaced with an AUTHORED sentence supplying the sense no line on the card had.
senses: to cheer on; to make an extra effort

hsk30l4/将.why: THE CARD GLOSSED A SENSE WHOSE READING IT DID NOT GIVE. Its gloss ended 'general, commander', which is 将 jiàng — and the card's Pinyin and bopomofo said jiāng and nothing else, so a reader was shown a meaning they could not have pronounced. CC-CEDICT gives the two readings apart; the second and third senses are added with the reading each belongs to, and all three of the card's own lines are the jiāng adverb.

hsk30l4/家庭.why: '大学里也有家庭作业吗？' is about HOMEWORK. 家庭作业 is a fixed word that swallows the headword, and its English called a 大学 a college besides. Replaced with an AUTHORED sentence, which the record says so is.

hsk30l4/加上.why: '“一个晚上，” 迪马加上。' uses 加上 as a verb of speech, which Chinese does not do — that is 补充 — and it carried a stray space after the closing quotation mark besides. Replaced with an AUTHORED sentence, which the record says so is.

AUTHORED, and the record says so; every row's reading and gloss was checked against CC-CEDICT before it was written.

hsk30l4/降低.why: '甚至在日落之后，气温也不见降低。' read 'there was little MODERATION in the temperature', which is not a thing anybody says.

hsk30l4/结果.why: THE GLOSS NAMED A SENSE BELONGING TO ANOTHER READING. 'result; outcome; fruit' — and the fruit is 结果 jiē guǒ, to bear fruit, which is a different word; the card's Pinyin says jié guǒ and nothing else, so a reader was shown a meaning they could not have pronounced. Batch 52 met this on 将 and fixed it by adding the reading; here the jiē guǒ word is not what a Level 4 vocabulary card is for, so the sense is dropped and the conjunction the card DOES lack is named instead.

hsk30l4/交.why: Labelled 'noun / verb' where 交 has no ordinary noun use at all — CC-CEDICT gives it as a verb throughout — so the label promised a sense that does not exist. | TWO OF ITS THREE LINES WERE COMPOUNDS THAT SWALLOW THE CHARACTER, and one of them had no business on a vocabulary card at all: 去医院要坐哪一路公交 is 公交, public transport, and 她不喜欢口交 is oral sex — a card glossed 'to hand over; to make friends' whose reader is shown that sentence has met the character in the one place it says nothing about the word. It is the class check-coarse.js exists for and one its own discriminator excuses, the headword being a single character contained in every compound built on it. Both replaced with AUTHORED sentences, which the record says so are. | '把钱交出来！' read 'Hand over the DOUGH!', which is a register nobody should be taught from a vocabulary card.
hsk30l4/交.gloss: to hand over; to pay; to make friends

hsk30l4/骄傲.why: Labelled 'noun / adjective' against a gloss that is only the adjective, and the card's own FIRST line is the noun: 骄傲使人落后 is pride making a person fall behind. | '骄傲使人落后。' was given the English proverb 'Pride goes before a fall', which says something else — the Chinese is half of 骄傲使人落后，虚心使人进步, pride making a person fall BEHIND others rather than come to grief — and it is also the card's only example of the noun.
exEn: 骄傲使人落后

hsk30l4/交流.why: Labelled a VERB and glossed with two NOUNS — 'exchange; communication'. Both are named properly now, and the tags say which of the card's lines is which.

hsk30l4/教育.why: Labelled 'noun / verb' against the single gloss 'education', so the verb had none. | '去历史系或者教育系。' is a fragment with no subject, and its 教育系 swallows the headword into a department name besides. Replaced with an AUTHORED sentence, which the record says so is.

hsk30l4/解释.why: Glossed 'to justify; explanation' under a verb label — to justify is 辩解, which is a claim about motives rather than about facts, and 'explanation' is a noun. All three of the card's own lines are the verb to explain.

hsk30l4/仅仅.why: Glossed 'barely', which is 勉强 — 仅仅 is only or merely, and the card's own translations say 'just' and 'only'. | A CHARACTER ERROR: '不能做仅仅是接口' wrote 接口, an interface, for 借口, an excuse — and the card's own English said 'excuse' all along, which is what settles it. hsk30l4/进行.why: Glossed 'advance; progress', neither of which is what any of the card's three lines does — 调查进行中 is an investigation under way, 按计划进行 is going to plan, 进行修改 is carrying a change out.
hsk30l4/进行.gloss: to carry out; to be under way

hsk30l4/节约.why: '我节约我有的钱。' is clumsy in both languages — the Chinese repeats 我 either side of the verb where a relative clause wants 我所有的钱, and the English read 'I save what money I got'. Replaced with an AUTHORED sentence, which the record says so is.

hsk30l4/郊区.why: Its first line ended in SIX ASCII FULL STOPS where Chinese sets an ellipsis as ……, two ellipsis characters. hsk30l4/交通.why: '这地方交通不方便。' read 'isn't convenient TO public TRANSPORTATION' — which is not English, and which is American besides. The corpus's two sites of that word are this one and 客运's gloss; two sites is not a table row.

hsk30l4/接受.why: '我们接受支票。' read 'We accept CHECKS', which is American — the decks write cheque thirteen times elsewhere, and `check` is deliberately absent from app.js's SPELL_PAIRS because 66 of its 73 sites are the ordinary verb. exEn: 我们接受支票

hsk30l4/仅.why: '嗯，仅此而已。' read 'YEA, that's all it is' — yea is an archaic word of assent and the sentence wants yeah.

hsk30l4/尽管.why: '你可以尽管放心。' read 'You can depend on it', which contains nothing a reader can match to 尽管; and 请尽管说 read 'please tell me' about helping 'your AREA' — 地方 there is a respect or a point, not a place.

hsk30l4/经济.why: Glossed 'economics' under a 'noun / adjective' label, and economics is 经济学 — a third word. The card's own lines are the ECONOMY (经济怎么样), the adjective ECONOMIC (经济实力) and the adjective ECONOMICAL (比大车经济), none of which is the discipline. Split and tagged.

hsk30l4/经历.why: Labelled 'noun / verb' against the single gloss 'experience', which is only the noun — the verb, to go through something, had none, and two of the card's three lines are that verb. | '我们俩都经历过不幸。' read 'WORSE THINGS have happened to both of us', which is a comparison the Chinese does not make — 经历过不幸 is having been through misfortune.

hsk30l4/竞争.why: Labelled a VERB and glossed only as one, where the card's second line is the NOUN — 精彩的竞争 is splendid competition.

hsk30l4/究竟.why: Labelled 'noun / adverb' against a gloss that is two adverb phrases — 'after all; when all is said and done' — so the noun, the ins and outs of a thing, had none; and all three of the card's own lines are the adverb meaning exactly or on earth, which the gloss did not give either.

hsk30l4/聚会.why: Labelled 'noun / verb' against a gloss that runs the two together — 'get together; meet; gathering'. hsk30l4/禁止.why: '禁止游戏吗？' is not a sentence anybody says — a bare 禁止 with no subject taking 游戏 as its object — and its English, 'Suspend the game?', is not what 禁止 means either. Replaced with an AUTHORED sentence, which the record says so is.

hsk30l4/就是.why: '不是你对的，就是我。' is ungrammatical: the 不是…就是… frame takes parallel predicates, so the 的 after 你对 has nothing to attach to and the second half has no predicate at all. Replaced with an AUTHORED sentence, which the record says so is. | '这就是生命。' read 'This is THE life', which in English means the good life — the Chinese says only that this is life.

exEn: 这就是生命

hsk30l4/聚.why: '我们好聚好散。' is the four-character idiom 好聚好散, to part on good terms — it swallows the character into a fixed phrase, and its English asserts a DIVORCE that is nowhere in the Chinese. hsk30l4/流.why: '我是个二流子。' is 二流子, a layabout — a fixed three-character word that swallows the headword, and a sentence that says nothing about flowing. Replaced with an AUTHORED sentence, which the record says so is.

Replaced with the verb and the attributive, which the card also lacked, leaving all three constructions distinct. The gloss `to need` is also widened to what CC-CEDICT gives. AUTHORED, and the record says so: short, ordinary, and using the word in the sense the card's own gloss gives it — and deliberately a DIFFERENT construction from the sentences already on the card, since a second example that repeats the first's shape teaches nothing the first did not.

hsk30l5/情感.why: A DEAD ONE-SIDED DISAMBIGUATOR. This card carried a `not <other word>` block answering a collision that no longer exists: the partner's gloss has since been sharpened by an earlier batch of this audit, so the two no longer share an English prompt and only this half of the pair still said they did. A collision is SYMMETRIC, so a hint one card carries and its named partner does not is a hint that is already dead — and a disambiguator that disambiguates nothing is worse than none, a reader taking it for a real distinction. Seventeen were found by sweeping the decks for it and every one was dead. NOTHING IN THE PIPELINE REPORTS THIS: check-mandarin-coverage.js counts the groups that DO share a gloss and whether each carries a disambiguator; it never asks whether a disambiguator points at a card that no longer collides. The hint cannot simply be deleted from this record either — the applier WRITES a hint where the record has one and never strips one the generator shipped — so it is retired by rewriting the gloss, which rebuilds the English field; and the gloss wanted rewriting anyway, every one of the seventeen being the thin one-word original the partner had already outgrown.

hintsWhy: AUTHORITATIVE: this map is the complete list of `not X` blocks in the Mandarin decks, including the 104 pairs the generator itself produced — it is regenerated from the finished decks, so a pair that stops colliding loses its block rather than keeping one that points at nothing. The English → Chinese card's front is the gloss and nothing else, so two notes sharing one are a question with two right answers. These are the 251 PAIRS that had no disambiguator; each member is given the deck's own `not <other word>` block, the shape 104 pairs already carry. A group of three or more is not hinted — naming four of five answers on the front is worse than the ambiguity — and is given a distinguishing gloss in `notes` instead. | Batch 83: SEVENTEEN DEAD ONE-SIDED HINTS RETIRED. A `not <other word>` block answers a COLLISION, and a collision is symmetric — so wherever one card of a pair carries the block and its named partner does not carry the reverse, the pair has already been separated and the survivor is disambiguating nothing. Found while repairing 动手, whose `not 上班` had outlived a rewrite of 上班's own gloss. Swept: 17 of 661 hinted cards were one-sided, and every one of the seventeen was dead — in each case the PARTNER's gloss had been sharpened by an earlier batch of this audit (书 `not 本子` against a 本子 rewritten to `a notebook; an exercise book`, 茶 `not 茶叶` against `tea leaves; tea`, 体力 `not 力气` against `muscle power, the strength to lift or push`). TWO of the seventeen were not in this record at all — 体力 and 顺利, shipped by the generator — which is the other half of the finding: THE APPLIER WRITES A HINT AND NEVER STRIPS ONE, so deleting a row here does not take a block off a deck. A dead hint is retired by rewriting the gloss, which rebuilds the English field. Re-run the one-sided sweep after any batch that rewrites a gloss.

decks.why: A learner met nine decks presented as nine levels with nothing to say where to start, how big each was against the others, or where the two decks outside the ladder fit. The Collections page prints this line under the deck's title. It replaces a subtitle that restated the word count and the direction, both of which the row already shows for itself. | `exBritish` is set on all nine decks: the British-spelling pass described in mandarin-fix.js, applied to every gloss and every example translation from app.js own SPELL_PAIRS.

hsk30l1.subtitle: The first 300 words — start here if you are new to Chinese
hsk30l1.why: A single-character card's Characters block glosses the character and stops there, and the tap panel that lists the other words built on it (openCharWin / charNeighbours in app.js) can only search the deck the reader has DOWNLOADED — measured on this deck, 71 of its 137 single-character cards have no other word in it at all, so for 52% of them the panel says "No other word in this deck uses it". `Compounds` is the authored answer, bounded by the language rather than by the deck. It is added to the type's field list, to the template on BOTH cards (after the Characters block, before the Examples fold) and to the type's own scoped CSS in one place, since a field added to only two of those three is stored and never shown. The rows are written compactly in each note's `compounds` and expanded by mandarin-fix.js. | A Chinese sentence takes Chinese punctuation, and 551 of the decks own example sentences were punctuated with ASCII marks — 我明年想学汉语. and 你们公司几点下班? and 我们出去后, 再也没有回来。 — so a card teaching Chinese showed a beginner the wrong marks for it. Deck-level rather than an entry per note, for the reason the Spanish record’s `exBritish` is: there is no judgement in it, and a mechanical substitution written out per card is one that gets applied to 116 cards and forgotten on the 117th. It CONVERTS a mark and never ADDS one: 130 of those sentences simply stop, and supplying a terminal is a claim that the sentence is complete, which a machine cannot make — those are read and repaired by hand, batch by batch.

It CONVERTS a mark and never ADDS one: 130 of those sentences simply stop, and supplying a terminal is a claim that the sentence is complete, which a machine cannot make — those are read and repaired by hand, batch by batch. | Level 3's card type gained the **`Compounds`** field, copied from Level 2's own definition in this record rather than retyped — the same anchor, markup and scoped CSS — so a change to one reaches all three levels that now carry it. A field added in one place and not the other two stores the value and shows it nowhere.

decks.whyFields: An idiom's gloss says what it MEANS and throws away what it SAYS, which is the picture that makes a four-character idiom memorable: 谢天谢地 is 'thank goodness' and it says 'thank heaven, thank earth'. The Literally line is added to the Chinese → English card, under the meaning.
decks.whyCredit: The decks' example sentences come from Tatoeba and carried no attribution — 60% of the 20,010 shipped sentences are verbatim in Tatoeba's own Mandarin-English pairs, and Tatoeba is CC BY 2.0 FR, which requires credit. Added to every deck's description, which is what the Collections page and the Studio show.
